problems.desc: Part (b): the sketched curve. A correct sketch starts at the marked point, follows the printed segments in both directions without crossing any of them, and stays smooth; it should flatten where the segments are horizontal and steepen where they are steep. Award full credit when the curve is tangent to the field everywhere it is drawn, and no credit for a curve that cuts across the segments.

Part (b): the sketched curve and its shape. A correct response draws a curve through the marked point that is tangent to the segments throughout and describes it as an arc of a circle centred at the origin, curving down to the right and down to the left. Award full credit only when the description matches the sketch; a tangent curve with no description, or a description with no sketch, is half.

Part (c): the sketched particular solution. A correct sketch is an upward parabola through the marked point whose tangent direction matches the printed segments at every height, flattening at the vertical axis and steepening to either side. Award full credit when the drawn curve agrees with the field and passes through the given point.

Part (b): telling the two equations apart. A correct response says that in the printed field the slope depends only on the height: every segment in a horizontal row is parallel, and the row along the horizontal axis is flat. That is what a slope of y looks like; a slope of x would give parallel segments in each vertical column instead, flat along the vertical axis. Full credit needs the row-versus-column observation, not just the correct choice.

Part (c): the sketched particular solution. A correct sketch rises through the marked point on the vertical axis, is flat exactly where the printed segments are flat, and grows ever more steeply to the right. Award full credit when the curve is tangent to the field throughout and does not cross the horizontal axis.

Part (b): the long-run behaviour. A correct response reads from the field that between the two equilibrium heights every segment slopes upward, so a solution starting below the upper equilibrium rises toward it and levels off without reaching it. Full credit needs both the rising behaviour and the levelling off at the upper equilibrium value.

Part (c): the sketch and the agreement. A correct response draws the particular solution through the marked point, tangent to the printed segments, and then states one specific way the drawing matches the field, for example that the curve steepens as it moves right because the slope grows with x, or that it flattens as the height grows because the slope is divided by y. Full credit needs a named feature, not a general claim that they agree.
